title: Article 144A — Special provisions as to disposal of questions relating to constitutional validity of laws (Omitted)

content.overview: Article 144A required a minimum number of Supreme Court judges for deciding the constitutional validity of Central or State laws. It was inserted by the 42nd Amendment and omitted by the Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977 (w.e.f. 13 April 1978) as part of the post-Emergency restoration of ordinary judicial process.
content.glance: Art 144A omitted by 43rd Amendment 1977 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978). Minimum-bench rule for constitutionality questions removed.
content.study:
Article 144A was an Emergency-era restriction on how the Supreme Court could dispose of constitutionality questions.

Omission: Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978), together with related omissions (31D, 32A, 131A, 226A, 228A).

Living frame: Supreme Court composition and benches are governed by Articles 145 and practice directions; there is no living Article 144A minimum-judge rule.

Examination rule: Do not cite Article 144A as a current procedural requirement.

sections.heading: Constitutional status
sections.body: Inserted by the 42nd Amendment; omitted by the 43rd Amendment, 1977 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978). Part of the package restoring pre-Emergency judicial review capacity.

misconceptions.trap: Article 144A still fixes the minimum bench for constitutionality cases.
misconceptions.correction: Article 144A was omitted by the 43rd Amendment, 1977. It is not living law.
